find.description: Find issues of the bound GitLab project by text, semantic state and labels, oldest first, one bounded page at a time. GitLab filters on state, labels and text in title and description; states map to labels through settings.states, and a closed issue is canceled by a canceled label or a duplicate link.

get.description: Read one issue of the bound GitLab project by its iid.

create.description: Open an issue in the bound GitLab project. The idempotency key is recorded in the description as a hidden comment: a repeated key returns the issue it opened, the same key with other content is a conflict, and a create whose outcome is unknown is read back and answered unresolved rather than opened twice. Only an issue the credential's account opened answers for a key; two concurrent calls with one key are not detected.

update.description: Change an issue's title, description or labels. Labels replace the task's labels; state labels change only through transition. expectedRevision is compared with the issue read just before the write: GitLab has no conditional issue write, so a writer between the two is not detected.

transition.description: Move an issue to a semantic state: the state labels settings.states names are swapped, and the issue is closed for done and canceled and reopened otherwise. A state other than open and done without a configured label is unsupported. expectedRevision is compared with the issue read just before the write.

assign.description: Replace an issue's assignees, named by username; @me names the credential's account. GitLab keeps only the users it can assign, one on a tier without multiple assignees, and the answer lists the actual assignees. An assignee is information, never an exclusive claim: this provider offers no claim.
